PullRequest.Title: Fix worktree creation display for peer chats
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request addresses the issue of displaying worktree creation notifications for peer chats, aligning their behavior with that of main chats. 

### Changes Made
- Peer-chat worktrees are now correctly associated with their owning chat in `sessionAdditionalWorktrees.ts`.
- The association is persisted before the peer chat is created, as implemented in `sessionServerTools.ts` and `agentService.ts`.
- The `WorktreeAnnouncementContribution` now:
  - Emits the localized "Created isolated worktree..." markdown used by main chat.
  - Displays this message exactly once in the owning peer chat.
  - Restores the message when chat history is reopened.
  - Prevents incorrect display in chats that reuse the worktree.

### Validation
- Focused regression tests were added and successfully passed.
- Targeted transpilation and type-checks for changed files are clean.
- Full type-check issues are unrelated to this change, stemming from missing Electron typings.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added call is reached for every non-default outgoing turn until an announcement is emitted, and `_findOwnedWorktree` is directly shown to call `tryOpenDatabase` plus `getMetadata`; the contribution dispatcher awaits it serially before `agent.chats.sendMessage`. For the common peer chat that does not own a newly-created additional worktree, the miss is never memoized, so this repeats deterministically. Exact disk latency varies by filesystem and SQLite contention, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem stat calls, SQLite metadata reads, JSON parsing/validation, and array scans
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For each non-owner peer chat, cost grows with every outgoing turn and every hydration/history-refresh event; each event performs one stat and one SQL query, while CPU/allocation also grows with the number of additional-worktree records in the session.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated critical-path I/O increases prompt-dispatch latency and background history-refresh I/O.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Peer-chat outgoing turns did not execute this contribution or access additional-worktree metadata; peer-chat hydration also returned without storage I/O.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every non-default outgoing turn first checks an in-memory positive-only memento, then performs a durable ownership lookup when it is false; misses do not change the memento and are retried indefinitely.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Before the diff, non-default chats returned immediately from `onHydrateTurns` and this contribution had no `onOutgoingTurn`, so ordinary peer-chat sends performed no additional-worktree storage lookup. The added RIGHT line 59 now places that lookup on every non-default outgoing-turn path unless the positive announcement state was reached.
Findings.Title: Cache negative worktree-ownership lookups
Findings.Impact: Sending messages in any ordinary peer chat now waits for a filesystem stat and SQLite metadata query before the prompt can reach the provider. Subscribed provider-history refreshes also repeat the lookup. On slower or contended storage this adds recurring send latency and unnecessary disk/SQLite activity even though ownership cannot appear after the chat has been created through this flow.
Findings.Evidence: `onOutgoingTurn` awaits `_findOwnedWorktree` at the added line. That helper calls `readSessionAdditionalWorktrees`, which invokes `ISessionDataService.tryOpenDatabase` (an awaited filesystem `stat` even when the DB is already warm), executes `SELECT value FROM session_metadata WHERE key = ?`, parses and validates the complete JSON array, then scans it. `AgentHostChatContributions.outgoingTurn` awaits contributions sequentially, and `AgentSideEffects` awaits that result immediately before provider dispatch. The same uncached helper is also reached from peer-chat hydration/history refresh. Only successful ownership plus metadata sets `announcementEmittedKey`; a non-owner leaves it false forever.
Findings.Recommendation: Memoize the ownership resolution, including `undefined`, per chat (or load a session-level chat-to-worktree map once) and clear it with the existing chat/session contribution lifecycle. Association is persisted before chat creation in this PR, so a chat created through this path can safely retain the negative result; preserve an explicit invalidation path if any other flow can associate an already-live chat.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a prompt from a peer chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After model selection and attachment resolution, all chat contributions run serially. The new worktree contribution must finish before `agent.chats.sendMessage`, so its ownership and first-announcement reads directly delay provider dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the parent session database path before acquiring the database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per non-default send while the positive announcement memento is false; repeated forever for non-owner chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This contribution did no work for peer-chat outgoing turns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SQLite SELECT of the additional-worktrees metadata, followed by JSON parse/validation and a chat scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per ownership lookup; the CPU/allocation portion scans all additional-worktree records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No additional-worktree metadata query occurred on peer-chat sends.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For the owning chat's first announcement, stat/open detached worktree metadata storage and probe worktree-path existence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once after a successful ownership lookup and announcement; retried on later sends if metadata is absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peer-chat sends did not read detached worktree metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read four detached worktree metadata keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for a successful first announcement; retried after metadata misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peer-chat sends had no detached metadata reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential Git worktree-root resolution through the Git service when the resolver's bounded path cache is cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the first successful metadata read for this path while cold; shared resolver caching removes repeat Git probes for known paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peer-chat announcement sends did not reach this metadata normalization path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can delay the first owning peer-chat send, but is bounded and required only for the one-time announcement path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Outgoing-turn count per peer chat. For chats that do not own a newly-created additional worktree, effective cardinality is one ownership lookup per send indefinitely; for the owner it is one successful lookup plus one detached-metadata load before the positive memento suppresses later sends.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Contribution execution is serial within each send. There is no coalescing of ownership misses across sends or chats; concurrent sends in different chats can issue independent storage reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The positive `announcementEmitted` state is cached per chat and cleaned up with chat/session contribution state. Negative ownership results and missing detached metadata are not cached, so warm sends repeat the same I/O. The Git primary-root resolver has its own bounded path cache, but it is reached only after a positive ownership lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed call path, awaited ordering, storage implementation, and positive-only cache behavior are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and SQLite latency depends on platform, cache warmth, and contention. The repeated critical-path boundary and its exact per-send cardinality are certain; only milliseconds and prevalence of long-lived peer chats vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: ordinary non-owner peer chats repeat a stat and SQLite query on every send because misses are not memoized.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial history restore gets provider messages and workspace transitions, then sequentially hydrates all contributions before returning turns. Subscribed `onDidChangeChatHistory` events likewise await hydration before state refresh; the new ownership lookup is therefore on both restore and refresh paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider history request occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pre-existing prerequisite that runs before contribution hydration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per peer-chat hydration or subscribed history refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Non-default hydration returned immediately from this contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds latency before restored/refreshed turns are published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read, parse, validate, and scan the complete additional-worktree metadata value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per peer-chat hydration or history refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No ownership metadata read on peer-chat hydration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds local I/O and CPU before history publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For an owning peer chat, stat/open detached worktree storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One for each owner hydration/history refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peer chats did not restore worktree announcements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to reconstruct the announcement before publishing turns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two metadata SELECTs, issued concurrently, for each owner hydration/history refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peer-chat hydration had no detached announcement reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to reconstruct the owner announcement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of peer chats restored and provider history-change events while subscribed. Effective cardinality is one parent-session ownership lookup per hydration event per peer chat; an owner adds one detached announcement lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hydration contributions are serial per chat. External history refreshes are sequenced per chat, but different chat keys can proceed independently; there is no session-level lookup coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Neither positive nor negative ownership is reused by `onHydrateTurns`; every hydration re-reads the parent metadata. Database connections may be warm, but `tryOpenDatabase` still performs a filesystem stat. The detached announcement read also runs on every owner hydration to reconstruct synthetic history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the new local storage boundaries and sequential hydration placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider event frequency differs by implementation and active subscriptions. The added local lookup per hydration event is explicit; exact wall-clock impact and number of simultaneously open chats vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same uncached ownership mechanism is covered by the reported finding. Owner-only detached reads are behavior-required and bounded to one owner per worktree, so they do not warrant a separate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a current-session peer chat with a newly isolated worktree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Worktree preparation performs Git discovery/creation and records the worktree. The PR then serially associates the allocated chat by reading and rewriting session metadata before `createChat`, rename, and initial prompt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing Git repository/worktree discovery, branch selection, and detached worktree creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several Git operations once per new isolated worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Git/worktree preparation already occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dominates worktree preparation before chat creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing read and write of additional-worktree records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read and one write in the successful preparation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preparation already persisted the unassociated worktree record.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for the newly created worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No association callback or additional pre-create stat existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Now completes before chat allocation is committed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the record array, copy/update one record, and rewrite the serialized array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SELECT and one metadata write per newly-created worktree chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prepared unassociated record was not rewritten before chat creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before `accessor.createChat` and the initial prompt.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per newly-created additional worktree/peer chat; the metadata serialization size grows with the session's additional-worktree record count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing `_additionalWorktreeSequencer` serializes preparation, association, release, and related record changes per session. Different sessions can proceed independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The association read always uses `tryOpenDatabase`, so even a warm connection incurs a stat; no read cache is used. This is a one-time write path, not a recurring miss.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the callback is passed only when preparation created a worktree and is awaited before createChat.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Record counts and local storage latency vary, but this is one bounded metadata update next to substantially heavier worktree creation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added association I/O is one-time, per-session serialized, and necessary to persist ownership before the chat can emit its first turn; it is not a realistic independent regression relative to existing Git worktree creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use or restore the default chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Default chats continue directly to the existing worktree announcement restore behavior and skip the new ownership lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing default-session worktree notice storage lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per default-chat hydration, as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One existing restore-announcement read per default-chat hydration; unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing sequential contribution hydration behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing worktree notice storage behavior is unchanged; the new peer-chat memento and ownership lookup are bypassed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on the default-chat path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and traced worktree association, outgoing-turn, hydration/history-refresh, storage, Git, and lifecycle paths. Submitted one cache-lifecycle finding for repeated negative ownership reads on ordinary peer chats; no separate issue was justified for the bounded association write or required owner announcement restoration.
